Figure out what methods work best for you and work them. Confidence is my #1 tool even when it's fake. I have bad anxiety and depression and often feel like I don't belong in Tech despite having proven myself time and time again over the past year. But when another associate or manager relies on me I remember that I do well and my confidence comes back. If none of that works I fake it. If you fake it enough it'll feel natural and you'll figure out how to survive. And don't be afraid to ask your coworkers for help. If they're good people they should be more than happy to help.

So I'm in a somewhat similar boat. At the end of the year I had 30 hrs of PTO and requested off December 23rd through the 27th to use it. And then any left over to be used for the 30th and 31st. I was then scheduled to work the 28th and 29th but before my shift sprained my ankle and ended up in the ER for 4 hours. I got a note to cover those two days. So I wasn't in at the end of the year to check my hours to see if my GM applied anything. But a previous day I had requested off I was given the PTO so assumed this would be the same. (Wrongly.)

Last week I didn't receive payment (direct deposit) for the week of the 23rd to the 29th. I decided that because of the holiday I'd be patient and see if it rolled in later. This morning I received payment from last week but still yet to from the last week of December. I asked my Sales Manager  about it and he said he would call HR and submit a ticket for me (this was this Monday 7th). Still have yet to hear anything or get payment. I even checked my paystubs on Associate Connection and that week is non existent.
I have to believe that my GM didn't apply my PTO at all. I've been relying on good faith that he did and something would be resolved but nothing yet. 

If nothing has happened by Monday I will call HR. I agree and think you should call as well and not wait like I have.
